sites.functional_impact_measured: Etoposide (VP-16) resistance assay in HeLa cells: PRESERVED (functional protein). Immunofluorescence in intact (non-permeabilized) cells with anti-HA antibody: epitope detected on extracellular face.
sites.rationale: L2 explicitly states the HA epitope at position 1001 is on the extracellular side of the plasma membrane by IF in intact cells, and L1 confirms the tagged protein confers etoposide resistance. Python lookup of the numbered sequence confirms residue 1001 = D and residue 1002 = D, both within the extracellular span 993-1022. This is the best-evidenced site: longest extracellular loop, furthest from TM boundaries, dual validation (surface + function). Full-length MRP1/ABCC1 with HA epitope inserted at position 1001, expressed in HeLa cells. The extracellular loop 993-1022 (MSD3) is 30 residues long; position 1001 is 9 residues from the proximal TM boundary (992) and 22 from the distal (1023). N1006 is a glycosylation site 5 residues downstream.

sources.claim: The intracellular versus extracellular location of the HA epitopes present in biologically active MRP variants was then established in intact and permeabilized cells by immunofluorescence using an anti-HA antibody. Epitopes inserted at positions 1001 and 1222 were located on the extracellular side of the plasma membrane, while the epitope inserted at position 938 was located intracellularly. These results are consistent with a six TM rather than a four TM domain model for the membrane portion of the carboxy-terminal half of MRP.

sources.claim: Insertion of epitopes at positions 4, 163, 271, 574, and 653 produced functional proteins while insertions at positions 127, 417, 461, and 529 abrogated the capacity of MRP to confer drug resistance. Epitopes inserted at positions 4, 163, and 574 were localized extracellularly, whereas those inserted at positions 271 and 653 revealed an intracellular location. Although a single epitope inserted at position 461 was compatible with MRP function, it was inaccessible to the anti-epitope antibody and two copies of the tag at that site abrogated MRP function.

literature_notes: Five sites are supported by the ledger, all validated by HA epitope insertion in full-length ABCC1 expressed in HeLa cells (PMID 9334225 [L3] and PMID 9485377 [L1/L2]). Extracellular localization was confirmed by immunofluorescence in intact (non-permeabilized) cells; function was confirmed by etoposide resistance. L4 (PMID 12146977) reports FLAG insertions in MSD1 and MSD3 extracellular loops with normal transport function, but names no specific residue numbers for the FLAG insertion positions, so it does not add new pinned sites beyond those already grounded in L2/L3; it does corroborate that extracellular loops of MSD1 and MSD3 tolerate epitope tags. Position 461 (extracellular span 461-464) was excluded from sites: L3 reports that a single HA copy was compatible with function but inaccessible to the anti-HA antibody, and two copies abrogated function — this is not a usable surface tag site. The N-glycosylation sites N17, N23 (in the 1-36 extracellular domain) and N1006 (in the 993-1022 loop) are noted as constraints for tag design near positions 4 and 1001 respectively.
